title: Submitting the capstone
idea: A final submission is a package a reviewer can check without you: the requirements, the diagrams, the running code, and tests that prove each requirement.
points: A short README says what the system does and how to run it.
Number each requirement and link it to the test that proves it.
Diagrams must match the code; update them after every late change.
A design notes section lists trade-offs, known limits and next steps.

hero.title: What goes in the package
head: Item
What it proves
Ready when
rows: One command runs the demo and tests
Class names match the code exactly
Each requirement has a passing check
Trade-offs and open limits are listed
hero.caption: Recurring bookings were a stretch goal: if you skipped them, say so in the design notes.

code.title: Requirements as checks
code.caption: Each check is named after a numbered requirement, so the run reads like a sign-off sheet. Add an R5 check (notify attendees) of your own.

walk.text: `Room` has a `capacity`; the repository and `StrictOverlapPolicy` are the c05-t04 classes.
A trimmed `BookingService` with the frozen c05-t01 API: `searchFree`, `book` and `cancel`, times in hours.
Each key names a requirement; each value asserts it holds.
The loop prints one pass line per requirement; a failed assert stops the run.

takeaway: Submit what a stranger can run, read and verify alone.
